transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-25
- Start: 15:00 PST
- Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood Product), Dana (Aurora Head of ML), Priya (Product), Omar (SRE), Ethan (Data Eng)

Summary: Short walkthrough of Redwood’s Eval / Monitor features (prompt sets, regression alerts, split/A-B benchmarking), combined with a proposed pilot for Aurora Retail focusing on checkout-assistant prompts and order-fulfillment quality. Discussed security needs (VPC, KMS, SOC2), pilot scope, and next steps.

00:00 Dana: Okay, uh, thanks everybody for joining. We wanted to get a feel for the eval tooling — we've been seeing drift in our checkout assistant lately and want a reliable way to detect regressions before they hit prod.
00:12 Maya: Great, thanks Dana. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE from Redwood, Luca and Noah are on to show the product. We'll run through prompt-set management, regression alerts, and also demo a split-benchmark or A/B comparison workflow.
00:24 Priya: Nice. Our immediate problem: some prompts yield hallucinated shipping dates or incorrect SKU matches. We need to measure that and set automated alerts.
00:34 Luca: Yep, understood. We'll show how you can map prompt-sets to evaluation metrics and then wire those into regression alerts with thresholds and guardrails. A couple things to flag up front: you can run evals via the Console or the Eval API, and results are exportable.
00:46 Omar: For us, networking / data residency is key — we prefer private deployment or VPC peering. Is there extra cost to keep logs for 12 months?
00:55 Noah: Short answer — retention and audit log retention are configurable; for Private deployments it's usually part of the enterprise tier, and for Hosted we offer add-on retention. We'll include the pricing options in the follow-up doc.
01:06 Dana: Walk us through a sample prompt-set.
01:12 Luca: Sure. In the Console you create a Prompt Set — name it, attach metadata tags (flow:checkout, model:llama-2-13b or whatever you're testing), upload canonical examples. You can also attach expected labels and a small rubric.
01:27 Luca: (screen-share) Here's a prompt-set for 'checkout-estimate' — we have 500 canonical examples, user messages and expected outputs. For each example we set an evaluation script, either a simple regex matcher, fuzzy SKU match, or custom JSON scorer.
01:45 Ethan: Quick Q — can we run our own scorer logic? We have a Python function that computes a weighted score across fields.
01:52 Luca: Yes, you can plug in a custom scoring function through the Eval API or run locally and push labels; Redwood accepts both. There's also a sandboxed lambda option if you want to run arbitrary code in the console.
02:05 Priya: How often do the regression alerts trigger? We want daily checks and immediate alerts for >5% drop in success rate.
02:13 Maya: You can configure evaluations to run on a schedule (daily/hourly) or on new commits to your prompt-set. Alerts can be threshold-based, rolling-window, or triggered on statistical significance tests.
02:27 Omar: Any false positives from small sample sizes? We need to avoid alert fatigue.
02:32 Luca: We have guardrails — minimum sample size, smoothing windows, and A/B split testing support so you can compare variants before escalating.
02:44 Dana: Show the A/B comparison workflow.
02:48 Luca: Sure. (screen-share) We set up a split — variant A uses your current LLM + prompt baseline, variant B uses new prompt rewrite + slightly different model config. We run a controlled traffic split or an offline batch evaluation. The UI shows side-by-side metrics: accuracy, token cost per request, latency p50/p95, and a difference column with confidence intervals.
03:11 Priya: Nice, can we compare cost tradeoffs? For example, B is better accuracy but costs 30% more.
03:18 Noah: Absolutely — we surface token costs and compute unit costs per outcome, so you can plot cost-per-success. There's also an optimizer that suggests batching / quant- profiles to hit a target cost.
03:30 Ethan: Can we include KV cache / prefix caching as a variable? Our context length varies a lot.
03:36 Luca: We expose configurations like cache TTL, grouping keys for prefix caching, and how the runtime handles KV cache warm vs cold. Those factors are included in the benchmark so you can see their impact on latency and cost.
03:49 Omar: Regarding security, we need to validate KMS and audit logs. We run monthly compliance audits.
03:55 Noah: For Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Audit logs are stored and can be forwarded to your SIEM. We also support SAML-based SSO and RBAC at the token and route level.
04:08 Priya: Any gotchas for on-prem?
04:11 Luca: Air-gapped installs require a break-glass process for patches; we'll coordinate. Performance parity depends on GPU type and kernel availability; we'll provide a shortlist of supported cards and recommended quantization profiles.
04:25 Dana: Let's get into an example regression: say our success metric is exact SKU match, and we drop from 92% to 84% overnight. How would Redwood surface root cause?
04:36 Luca: First, the regression alert would notify the defined Slack channel or email. Then the Eval dashboard correlates metric drops with recent model rollouts, prompt-set commits, or infra changes. You can run a pairwise diff to surface which examples flipped from pass->fail.
04:52 Priya: That pairwise diff is key for us. Can we annotate examples with tags (e.g., high-value customers) so those failures bubble up?
04:58 Luca: Yes — example metadata supports tags and importance weights; alerts can prioritize regressions on high-value shards.
05:08 Dana: If we see drift tied to model size changes, can we automatically fallback to a stable variant?
05:13 Maya: Yes, Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback policies. You can configure canary percentages, latency floors, and automatic rollbacks on metric degradation.
05:24 Omar: For the pilot we probably want to test both Hosted and Dedicated configs. Cost sensitivity is big — we need to know delta in token price vs reserved capacity.
05:33 Noah: We'll include a cost comparison in the follow-up — typically Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale but needs a commit; Hosted gives faster iteration. We'll show sample math for your traffic mix.
05:44 Priya: Can we run the initial 20k-token benchmark on Redwood's hosted first and then replicate on Dedicated?
05:49 Luca: Yes, that's exactly the path many customers take — quick hosted proof then Dedicated pilot. We'll provision a dedicated staging pool for the A/B run if you want.
06:00 Dana: How are evals stored and queried? We need to keep examples and full model outputs for audits.
06:05 Luca: Evals are stored in the console with metadata. You can export raw outputs or forward them to your data lake. For compliance we support retention rules per workspace.
06:15 Ethan: Will the outputs contain PII? We may need redaction.
06:19 Noah: We support post-process redaction pipelines before storage. Also, you can configure no-store on certain routes.
06:27 Priya: Walkthrough time — can you demo a prompt-set creation and a quick offline A/B?
06:32 Luca: Sure. (screen-share: Console) Step 1: create prompt-set 'checkout-canonical-v1' — upload CSV of 500 examples. Step 1.5: add expected label column 'sku_label' and a boolean for 'pass'. Step 2: define eval metric 'sku_match' (fuzzy) — we have a prebuilt fuzzy matcher and can show the threshold.
06:54 Luca: Step 3: create two variants — baseline (model: redwood-4b-quant) and variant-b (model: redwood-7b-fp16 + prompt rewrite). Set offline batch evaluation. Start job.
07:07 Luca: (job running) Results streaming: baseline accuracy 91.8% (p95 latency 180ms), variant-b accuracy 94.6% (p95 latency 240ms), cost delta +32%. Pairwise diff shows 18 examples flipped.
07:25 Priya: Can I click into an example that flipped and see the raw tokens?
07:29 Luca: Yep. (click) Here — example ID 000234: user asked 'when will my order arrive' — baseline said '3–5 business days' but missed the express shipping flag. Variant-b includes express parsing and returns the correct date. You can add a note or tag that example.
07:47 Dana: This UI is helpful. For the alerting side, show how we'd set a regression alert for >5% drop specifically on high-value customers.
07:55 Luca: Go to Alerts -> New Rule. Scope: workspace 'aurora-prod' (or staging), prompt-tag = 'high-value', metric = sku_match, condition = drop >=5% over 24h, samples >= 200, notify Slack channel #aurora-llm. You can also add a webhook to trigger an automated rollback.
08:20 Omar: What about false positives due to seasonal spikes? We have big holiday bursts.
08:25 Maya: Use calendar-aware windows or holiday-aware baselines; Redwood supports custom baseline windows and holiday suppression rules.
08:35 Priya: On A/B splits, can we route real traffic at a % or do we have to do offline?
08:40 Luca: You can do both. For live A/B we manage routing at the edge and collect per-variant traces with KV cache separation to avoid cross-contamination.
08:54 Ethan: If we do live split, will that affect our latency SLO? We can't have p95 double.
08:58 Luca: If variant B is heavier, you can set SLO gates in rollout policy to limit exposure or throttle traffic.
09:08 Dana: Let's talk acceptance criteria for the pilot. Our success metrics: reduce SKU false-match by 75% in pilot examples, maintain p95 latency under 300ms, and cost-per-correct under $0.03.
09:20 Maya: Good, we captured that — we'll codify these in the pilot scope.
09:25 Priya: Can you run an automatic sweep for prompt rewrites? We have internal prompt engineers who want automated suggestions.
09:31 Noah: We have a prompt-rewrite assist that proposes alternatives and scores them offline. It's not fully automated production rollout, but it gives a ranked list and you can A/B test the top picks.
09:43 Omar: Network question: VPC peering + private logs — what's the setup time?
09:47 Noah: Usually 2–4 weeks for Private with networking reviews; Hosted + VPC peering for logs can be faster but depends on your firewall rules. We'll run a network checklist in the SOC2 session.
09:58 Dana: Can you show me the API payload for running an ad-hoc eval?
10:02 Luca: Sure. (switch) The Eval API accepts a JSON array of examples, each with input, expected, and metadata. Send POST to /v1/evals with auth token. Response includes job id and streaming status. We'll paste a sample in the follow-up notes.
10:18 Priya: Ok, quick final Q: are model labels stable across runs? We sometimes see small differences for stochastic decoding.
10:25 Luca: Stochastic outputs vary, so evaluators use deterministic seeds or n-gram based comparators. For exact-match metrics we recommend deterministic generation; for fuzzy metrics we use tolerance thresholds.
10:36 Dana: Anything about legal / procurement? We may need standard terms and a DPA.
10:40 Maya: We have a standard DPA and enterprise T&Cs; legal can share a redline. Procurement timelines vary but we'll coordinate.
10:48 Priya: This has been useful. Any competitors you suggest we compare during the pilot?
10:53 Maya: Customers often run side-by-side with hosted endpoints from Anthropic or OpenAI for specific prompts; Redwood focuses on the serving + eval surface so we recommend including a model-provider baseline.
11:05 Luca: Demo wrap — to summarize: we showed prompt-set creation, offline A/B benchmark, pairwise diffs, alerts with thresholds and sample-size guardrails, and rollout/fallback options.
11:17 Dana: Recap from Aurora side: we'll share canonical prompt-set and label spreadsheet (Ethan), finalize pilot stakeholders (Dana), and evaluate both hosted then dedicated for production.
11:28 Maya: Great. We'll send the pilot scope and pricing and schedule the SOC2/network deep-dive.
11:35 Noah: I'll attach the example API snippets and a quick-run checklist.
11:39 Priya: Thanks — let's plan for a 2-week pilot start target.
11:43 Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
